core_obligations: Replacement reduction (proof lines 7222-7238): choose a K-flat quasi-isomorphism (B', d) to (B, d); the equivalence D(B', d) to D(B, d) with quasi-inverse restriction, which is canonically the derived tensor with B as a (B, B')-bimodule, reduces the statement to the three compositions D(A) to D(B) to D(B'), D(B') to D(B) to D(C), and D(A) to D(B') to D(C).

The two reduced compositions (proof lines 7239-7247): the first is lemma-compose-tensor-functors because B' is K-flat as a complex of R-modules; the second holds because B derived-tensor B equals B plain-tensor B equals B, so lemma-compose-tensor-functors-general applies; hence the case where B is K-flat remains.

K-flat case (proof lines 7249-7270): it suffices to show the plain-versus-derived comparison map of lemma-compose-tensor-functors-general-algebra is an isomorphism; choose a property-(P) resolution L to A, so P = L tensor_R B has property (P) as a differential graded B-module, and the required quasi-isomorphism P tensor_B (B tensor_R C) to (A tensor_R B) tensor_B (B tensor_R C) rewrites as P tensor_R B tensor_R C to A tensor_R B tensor_R C.

Closing the K-flat case (proof lines 7271-7281): since B is K-flat as a complex of R-modules, more-algebra-lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism reduces the rewritten map to P tensor_R C to A tensor_R C, which is quasi-isomorphic by the choice of L and the hypothesis that A tensor_R C represents the derived tensor.
proof_roadmap: Replace B by a K-flat quasi-isomorphic B' and reduce to three compositions through the equivalence and its restriction quasi-inverse.
Dispatch two of the compositions with the two composition lemmas, leaving the K-flat case.
Build the property-(P) resolution of A and rewrite the required map in tensor form.
Apply the K-flat quasi-isomorphism lemma to cut back to the assumed quasi-isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the composition of the two derived tensor functors through (B, d) is again a derived tensor with an (A, C)-bimodule (statement lines 7210-7227). The proof (lines 7229-7281) is a genuine reduction argument: a K-flat replacement of the intermediate algebra with its equivalence and restriction quasi-inverse, the dispatch of two of the three resulting compositions through the chapter's composition lemmas, and a final K-flat case where a property-(P) resolution and the rewriting of the comparison map hand the problem to the K-flat quasi-isomorphism lemma and the standing hypothesis. H2: the reduction architecture is the argument, and the final cut-back step composes three identifications non-trivially.
